title: [Keyboard Manager] the new editor doesn't show targeted process name for disabled chords

status.label: The disabled-list template omits the app label
status.detail: The screenshot shows app names on neighboring remappings but not under Disabled; current upstream MainPage.xaml confirms the disabled template has no AppName binding.

next_action.label: Approve the disabled-list app-label design
next_action.reason: Current source and the reporter's screenshot directly confirm that app-specific scope is not displayed in the disabled-chord list.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming that the process label is still missing in v0.100.2 and for noting the separate specificity problem after changing an app-specific disabled chord into a disabled key. The screenshot and current source confirm the missing list label; to keep the second behavior distinct, could you share the exact chord and target process name, the steps used to convert it to a disabled key, and the resulting behavior that shows the app scope was lost? Please include the current PowerToys version if you retest it.

judgment.rationale: The primary display defect is directly supported by the screenshot and current upstream XAML: the remapping item templates bind AppName, while the DisabledList item template displays the shortcut and controls without any AppName binding. A separate comment reports a specificity regression after converting an app-specific disabled chord to a disabled key; that is not proven to share the display defect and needs its own concrete repro.
evidence: The report provides a v0.99.1 repro with an app-specific disabled chord and includes a screenshot plus a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP.
The screenshot shows the app label 'matlab' beside neighboring app-specific remappings, while the entries in the Disabled section have no app label.

Current upstream main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 binds AppName in the regular remapping list template but not in the DisabledList template in src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml.
A commenter says the label omission persists in v0.100.2 and separately reports that converting an app-specific disabled chord to a disabled key breaks specificity.
No assignee or direct fix PR was found for #47961.
judgment.recommended_action: Add the target-app label to disabled-list rows and separately collect a precise repro for the reported app-specific conversion regression.

fix_assessment.rationale: The disabled-list rendering is confirmed to omit AppName even though the same Remapping model and the regular remapping templates expose it. The separate key-conversion symptom is not included in this fix without a reproducer.

proposed_fixes.title: Show app scope on disabled shortcut rows
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The DisabledList DataTemplate in MainPage.xaml renders the shortcut and toggle but has no AppName display binding, unlike the regular remapping template. As a result, app-specific disabled chords appear indistinguishable from all-app disabled chords.
plan: Add the same conditional app-name label used by the regular remapping item template to the DisabledList item template.
Keep the label bound to the disabled Remapping.AppName value and hidden for all-app entries.
Add or extend a UI test with one app-specific disabled chord and one all-app disabled chord to verify that only the scoped entry shows its process name.
Verify that editing, toggling, and deleting disabled entries still behave as before.
verification: An app-specific disabled chord shows its target process name in the Disabled section.
An all-app disabled chord does not show a misleading process label.
The existing screenshot repro passes and the disabled mapping's saved app scope is unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The omission is explicit in the current upstream DisabledList template and matches the supplied screenshot; a narrowly scoped display binding addresses the reported primary defect.

issue_context.summary: The new Keyboard Manager editor does not show the target process name beside app-specific disabled chords, and a commenter separately reports an app-scope regression when converting a disabled chord to a disabled key.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys v0.99.1 and supplies numbered steps for creating app-specific remap and disable entries.
The issue includes a screenshot and a diagnostic ZIP; the screenshot shows 'matlab' beside app-specific remappings, while disabled rows show no process label.
A commenter confirms the missing process label in v0.100.2 and separately says converting an app-specific disabled chord to a disabled key breaks specificity.
Current upstream main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 renders AppName in regular remapping rows but not in the DisabledList template.
No assignee or linked fix PR was found for #47961.
inferences: Because both list templates bind the same Remapping model but only the regular template renders AppName, the primary defect is a presentation omission rather than evidence that the underlying app scope was lost.
The app-scope loss after converting a disabled chord may be a separate persistence or conversion defect; the comment does not provide enough steps to assign it to the same code path.
issue_context.analysis: The process-label defect is implementation-ready without requesting another diagnostic archive: the reporter already supplied a screenshot and ZIP, and current upstream XAML confirms the missing binding. Keep the separate conversion/scope complaint as an independent evidence gap rather than expanding the proposed display fix.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and the comment, including the v0.100.2 persistence claim and the separate disabled-chord-to-key specificity claim.
Inspected the supplied screenshot; it shows app labels for neighboring remappings and no label on rows under Disabled.
Read current upstream MainPage.xaml at commit 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368; the disabled-row template contains no AppName binding while regular remapping rows do.
Compared closed #46240, which was fixed by #46377 and released in v0.99.0 for creating disabled keys/shortcuts; it does not cover displaying target-app scope on disabled rows.
Compared #49352 and #48541; they describe distinct duplicate physical backslash key identity problems, not disabled-row app labels.

information_gaps.information: The exact chord and target process, steps to convert the app-specific disabled chord into a disabled key, and the resulting behavior that demonstrates loss of app scope
information_gaps.why_needed: The comment describes a second possible bug independent of the confirmed label omission; a precise repro is needed before recommending a separate persistence or conversion fix.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest the conversion on the current editor and provide the source chord, process name, PowerToys version, and which applications still have the key disabled afterward.
